deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the draft of Riemann's 1851 Göttingen dissertation, 'Grundlagen für eine allgemeine Theorie der Functionen einer veränderlichen complexen Grösse'. It continues §5, where T is a surface spread over the plane, possibly with several sheets. The page finishes the local analysis of branch points and begins §6, on connectivity.

(1) Local monodromy at a branch point. Take a directed line l and an exceptional point σ on it. On the left of l lie sheets a_1..a_n; on the right lie a'_1..a'_n.
- Above σ, a'_i is glued to a_i.
- Below σ, a'_i is glued to a_{α_i}, where (α_1..α_n) is a permutation of (1..n). In modern terms there is a permutation π with π(i)=α_i.
- Follow a point that starts in a_1 and crosses l above σ into a'_1. When it crosses back to the left below σ, it lands in a_{α_1}.
- So one full loop around σ sends sheet i to sheet π(i). Repeated loops visit the sheet indices 1, π(1), π²(1), …, μ, π(μ), …

(2) Why the orbit is a cycle. Riemann argues that the terms are pairwise distinct until 1 recurs. Any middle term α_μ is uniquely preceded by μ, and so on back to 1. Modern restatement: π is injective, so the first repetition in the sequence π^k(1) must be a return to 1.
- Hence after some m ≤ n steps 1 recurs, and the sequence is then periodic with period m.
- Thus the orbit of 1 is a cycle of length m. The circling point returns to its starting sheet after exactly m circuits and is confined to these m sheets.
- These m sheets join over σ into a single point. Riemann calls it a 'Windungspunkt (m−1)-ter Ordnung', i.e. a branch point of order (ramification index minus one) m−1.
- Applying the same procedure to the other n−m sheets decomposes them into further cycles of lengths m_1, m_2, … (sheets not branched at σ are fixed points). Hence branch points of orders m_1−1, m_2−1, … may also lie over the same point σ.
- In modern terms: the local monodromy permutation splits into disjoint cycles, and each cycle of length k is one point of T over σ with ramification index k.

(3) §6, connectivity definitions.
- Two parts of the surface are 'zusammenhängend' (connected) if some path through the interior joins them. Modern term: path-connected.
- A Querschnitt (cross-cut) is defined in the revised version as a simple arc through the interior, passing no point twice, running from one boundary point to a boundary point. This replaces a struck-out first version that lacked the simplicity condition.
- A connected surface is 'einfach zusammenhängend' (simply connected) if every cross-cut disconnects it; otherwise it is 'mehrfach zusammenhängend' (multiply connected).
- The page ends by announcing theorems on successive cutting by cross-cuts. These are given on the next page and lead to the connectivity number.
errors: No mathematical errors. The distinctness argument is a compressed but correct injectivity argument: if the first repeated term were some π^j(1) with j>0, then its predecessor would also repeat earlier, a contradiction.

Minor imprecision: the bound on m is just m ≤ n. The phrase 'die offenbar ≤ n sein muss' (which obviously must be ≤ n) is fine. m=1 (no branching) is allowed implicitly and corresponds to a 'Windungspunkt 0-ter Ordnung', i.e. an ordinary point.
The struck-out first definition of Querschnitt did not require the arc to be simple. The insertion 'keinen Punkt mehrfach' (no point more than once) correctly repairs this.

results.what: Local monodromy around a branch point: the gluing permutation of sheets decomposes into cycles. Each cycle of length m gives a branch point of order m−1 where m sheets meet in one point; several branch points can lie over the same base point.
results.modern_name: Cycle decomposition of local monodromy; ramification index / branch point order of a branched covering (Riemann surface)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann, Dissertation 1851 (Windungspunkt), later Puiseux/Hurwitz in the monodromy-group formulation

results.what: Definition of cross-cut (Querschnitt) and of simply vs multiply connected surfaces via cross-cuts
results.modern_name: Simply connected surface; cross-cuts and connectivity order (first Betti number)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann 1851 dissertation and 1857 Abelian functions paper

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a draft of §5–6 of Riemann's published 1851 dissertation. Windungspunkte and Querschnitte are famously his. The only extra information is draft-level wording, such as the revised, more precise definition of Querschnitt.

checkable.sympy: from sympy.combinatorics import Permutation; p=Permutation([1,2,0,4,3,5]); sorted(len(c) for c in p.cyclic_form)+[1]*(p.size-p.support().__len__())
checkable.asserts: The sheet permutation splits into disjoint cycles (here lengths 3,2,1) whose lengths sum to n=6.

checkable.sympy: from sympy.combinatorics import Permutation; p=Permutation([1,2,0,4,3,5]); p.size - p.cycles == sum(len(c)-1 for c in p.full_cyclic_form)
checkable.asserts: The total branch order over the point, Σ(m_i−1), equals n minus the number of points over σ (number of cycles).

checkable.sympy: from sympy.combinatorics import Permutation; p=Permutation([1,2,0,4,3,5]); (p**3)(0)==0 and all((p**k)(0)!=0 for k in range(1,3))
checkable.asserts: The point starting in sheet 1 returns after exactly m=3 circuits (orbit length of 1 equals its cycle length).

transcription_corrections: The base point is written 'b' throughout the transcription, but the manuscript symbol (resembling '6') is σ, consistent with the previous page ('eines solchen Punktes σ'). Read σ for b everywhere.
The struck-out phrase '[-ist dann auf m-]' is correctly marked; the image shows 'ist dann auf' struck through with an 'm' below it.

The struck-out first definition of Querschnitt is correctly identified. The marginal replacement reads 'd. h. eine das Innere einfach – keinen Punkt mehrfach – von einem Begrenzungspunkte bis zu einem Begrenzungspunkte durchschneidende Linie'.
